title: What are the use cases of flatMap() (flatten nested collections, split to multiple values, Optional::stream, stream of streams, nested data)?
shortTitle: flatMap use cases — flatten nested collections, split values, Optional::stream, nested data

s1_definition.profdef: flatMap has 5 core use cases: (1) FLATTEN NESTED COLLECTIONS — `List<List<Trade>>` → `Stream<Trade>`, (2) SPLIT ONE VALUE TO MANY — one CSV line → multiple tokens, one sentence → multiple words, (3) OPTIONAL::STREAM — extract present values from `Stream<Optional<T>>`, removing empties, (4) STREAM OF STREAMS — merge multiple stream sources into one, (5) NESTED DATA STRUCTURES — customer → accounts → trades → fees (multi-level flatten). In each case, flatMap takes a function that returns a Stream and merges all resulting streams into one flat stream.
s1_definition.analogy: flatMap is the bank's ENVELOPE OPENER. (1) A bag of envelopes, each containing multiple cheques → flatMap opens each envelope and puts all cheques on one belt. (2) A corporate cheque "Pay Rs.50000 to Rajesh,Priya,Amit" → flatMap splits it into 3 individual cheques. (3) Some envelopes are empty (Optional.empty) → flatMap discards them and only forwards envelopes with cheques. (4) Three departments each have their own stack of cheques → flatMap merges all stacks into one. (5) A holding company → subsidiaries → branches → transactions → flatMap drills down each level.
s1_definition.oneliner: flatMap = open, expand, flatten. Nested collections → flat. CSV → tokens. Optional → value or gone. Multiple sources → merged. Multi-level → drilled down.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** flatMap has 5 core use cases: (1) FLATTEN NESTED COLLECTIONS — `List<List<Trade>>` → `Stream<Trade>`, (2) SPLIT ONE VALUE TO MANY — one CSV line → multiple tokens, one sentence → multiple words, (3) OPTIONAL::STREAM — extract present values from `Stream<Optional<T>>`, removing empties, (4) STREAM OF STREAMS — merge multiple stream sources into one, (5) NESTED DATA STRUCTURES — customer → accounts → trades → fees (multi-level flatten). In each case, flatMap takes a function that returns a Stream and merges all resulting streams into one flat stream.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** flatMap is the bank's ENVELOPE OPENER. (1) A bag of envelopes, each containing multiple cheques → flatMap opens each envelope and puts all cheques on one belt. (2) A corporate cheque "Pay Rs.50000 to Rajesh,Priya,Amit" → flatMap splits it into 3 individual cheques. (3) Some envelopes are empty (Optional.empty) → flatMap discards them and only forwards envelopes with cheques. (4) Three departments each have their own stack of cheques → flatMap merges all stacks into one. (5) A holding company → subsidiaries → branches → transactions → flatMap drills down each level.

**One line to remember:** flatMap = open, expand, flatten. Nested collections → flat. CSV → tokens. Optional → value or gone. Multiple sources → merged. Multi-level → drilled down.

sections.s2_technical:
```java
// USE CASE 1: Flatten nested collections
List<List<String>> departments = List.of(
    List.of("Rajesh", "Priya"),    // Savings dept
    List.of("Amit", "Deepa"),      // Loans dept
    List.of("Vikram")              // Forex dept
);
List<String> allEmployees = departments.stream()
    .flatMap(Collection::stream)   // List<List<String>> → Stream<String>
    .toList();                      // [Rajesh, Priya, Amit, Deepa, Vikram]

// USE CASE 2: Split one value into many
List<String> allSymbols = List.of("RELIANCE,TCS,HDFC", "INFY,WIPRO")
    .stream()
    .flatMap(csv -> Arrays.stream(csv.split(",")))  // 2 strings → 5 strings
    .toList();  // [RELIANCE, TCS, HDFC, INFY, WIPRO]

// USE CASE 3: Optional::stream (Java 9)
List<String> presentValues = List.of(
    Optional.of("RELIANCE"), Optional.empty(), Optional.of("TCS")
).stream()
    .flatMap(Optional::stream)     // present → Stream.of(v), empty → Stream.empty()
    .toList();                      // [RELIANCE, TCS]

// USE CASE 4: Merge multiple stream sources
Stream<String> merged = Stream.of(
    trades.stream().map(Trade::getSymbol),
    holdings.stream().map(Holding::getSymbol),
    watchlist.stream()
).flatMap(s -> s);                 // Stream<Stream<String>> → Stream<String>

// USE CASE 5: Multi-level nested drill-down
List<Fee> allFees = customers.stream()
    .flatMap(c -> c.getAccounts().stream())      // customers → accounts
    .flatMap(a -> a.getTrades().stream())         // accounts → trades
    .flatMap(t -> t.getFees().stream())           // trades → fees
    .toList();                                     // all fees across all customers
```
sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank's compliance report needs to collect ALL transaction tags across ALL transactions across ALL accounts for a customer.** The data model: Customer → multiple Accounts → multiple Transactions → multiple Tags. Three levels of nesting. Without flatMap: `Stream<List<List<List<String>>>>`. With flatMap: `Stream<String>`.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 — UC1 (3-level flatten).** 2 customers → flatMap → 3 accounts → flatMap → 6 transactions → flatMap → 18 tags. Three levels of nesting collapsed into one flat stream.

**Step 2 — UC3 (Optional).** 6 transactions, each with Optional<String> riskNote. 4 are empty, 2 have values. flatMap(Optional::stream) → 2 risk note strings. Empty Optionals silently vanish.

**Step 3 — UC2 (split).** "RELIANCE,TCS,HDFC" → split(",") → ["RELIANCE","TCS","HDFC"]. flatMap turns 1 string into 3 strings.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ 5 USE CASES OF flatMap ═══

  UC1: FLATTEN NESTED COLLECTIONS
    Customer → [Account1, Account2]
    Account1 → [Txn1, Txn2, Txn3]     3 levels of nesting
    Txn1 → [TAG1, TAG2, TAG3]
    flatMap × 3 → [TAG1, TAG2, TAG3, TAG4, ...TAG18]  FLAT!

  UC2: SPLIT ONE TO MANY
    "RELIANCE,TCS,HDFC" ──split(",")──→ ["RELIANCE", "TCS", "HDFC"]
    flatMap: 1 string → 3 strings

  UC3: OPTIONAL::STREAM
    Optional.of("note") ──Optional::stream──→ Stream.of("note")  → "note"
    Optional.empty()     ──Optional::stream──→ Stream.empty()     → (gone)

  UC4: MERGE STREAMS
    Stream.of(stream1, stream2, stream3)
    .flatMap(s → s) → one merged stream

  UC5: ONE-TO-MANY EXPANSION
    3 ──flatMap──→      (generate 3)
    1 ──flatMap──→        (generate 1)
    0 ──flatMap──→ (empty)  (generate 0)
    Result:   (4 stars from 3 inputs)
```
sections.s5c_hld:
HLD is the big-picture view. In National Bank of India's portfolio-aggregation service, `flatMap()` flattens nested structure: one customer has many accounts, each account has many transactions, so `customers.stream().flatMap(c -> c.accounts().stream()).flatMap(a -> a.txns().stream())` produces one flat transaction stream for reporting. It also powers `Optional::stream` to drop empties and split comma-separated instrument lists. The stateless service reads the nested object graph from PostgreSQL, flattens in memory, and caches the flat report in Redis.

```

  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
  │Portfolio │ │Scheduler │  ← Client Layer
  │   UI     │ │          │
  └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ HTTPS
       └──────┬──────┘
              ▼
       ┌──────────────┐
       │ API Gateway  │ JWT, rate limit
       └──────┬───────┘ REST
              ▼
    ┌───────────────────────────┐
    │ Aggregation Service (×4)  │ flatMap nested graph → flat stream
    └───┬──────────────┬────────┘
  JDBC  │              │ Kafka
        ▼              ▼
  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
  │ PostgreSQL   │ │ Kafka audit  │→ ELK
  │ cust/acct/txn│ └──────────────┘
  └──────┬───────┘
         ▼
  ┌──────────────┐
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
flatMap has five primary use cases in Java streams. First, flattening nested collections: when each element contains a collection (Account has List of Trades), flatMap opens each collection and merges all elements into one flat stream. Second, splitting one value into many: a CSV line split by comma produces an array, and flatMap(Arrays::stream) flattens all arrays into individual tokens. Third, extracting present Optional values: flatMap(Optional::stream) converts present Optionals to their values and removes empty ones, replacing the filter(Optional::isPresent).map(Optional::get) pattern. Fourth, merging multiple stream sources into one: Stream.of(stream1, stream2, stream3).flatMap(s -> s) produces a single merged stream. Fifth, multi-level drill-down: chaining multiple flatMaps drills through nested data structures — customer to accounts to trades to fees.

In my compliance tag service, I demonstrate the most powerful use case: 3-level nested drill-down. Two customers contain three accounts containing six transactions containing eighteen tags. Three chained flatMap calls — flatMap(c -> c.accounts().stream()), flatMap(a -> a.transactions().stream()), flatMap(t -> t.tags().stream()) — collapse the entire hierarchy into a flat Stream of String with all 18 tags accessible for distinct(), sorted(), and groupingBy(). Without flatMap, you would need three nested for-loops. With flatMap, it is a single declarative pipeline.
